name: target-input-journal-v1
scope: Synthetic public metadata and acceptance contract; not execution or device evidence.

identity.flutterLegacyBoundary: v1/v2 did not record herdr executable path; preserve this historical limitation explicitly instead of inventing a value

complete.effect: known outcome or proven unsent; exact active lease and raw record only

abandon.effect: retire only this active attempt; never remove durable record

resolve.effect: explicit reviewed original raw record only; reject while target active

rules: Persist before network write. Never store input bytes or replay unknown input.
One pending marker per durable remote target, shared across tabs and attempts.
Different targets may prepare independently; one target being active or unknown cannot clear or block an unrelated valid target.
Same-target active ownership lasts through asynchronous original-operation settlement. A late completion/abandon cannot retire a newer attempt.
Known server receipt and explicit human resolution are different operations; neither may delete a different request record.
Legacy single record remains bound to its original recorded identity. Do not fill missing identity fields using the currently selected host.
Migration preserves an original unknown record or fails closed; no automatic deletion, eviction, input retry, or silent corruption repair.
Corrupt/unsupported/oversized store is unavailable rather than empty. Persistent failure cannot silently unlock writes.
No implicit shared PTY resize or input focus transfer.

cases.scenario: A unknown, B different terminal can persist and write; resolving B leaves A byte-exact
Same target via two tabs cannot have concurrent writes or duplicate pending markers
A old receipt/abandon/resolve cannot clear or retire a newer A request
Manual resolution rejects an active write owned by another adapter or native instance
Legacy single v1/v2 becomes one original entry on mutation; no fields rebound
Changed route profile/revision/identity, host pin, host/user/socket/session/pane/terminal cannot clear old target
32-target and byte capacities reject new record without evicting existing unknown entries
Prepare times out after persistence; caller never submits/replays and preserves original ownership until settlement
Known receipt with local clear failure stays known-and-locked; unrelated target remains independent when storage is readable
Concurrent prepare/clear conflicts preserve all unrelated records and exact request binding
After process restart no active request is assumed; durable unknown requires original target new full and explicit review
